sources.note: Describes Tegem (Lafofa), not Amira; pp.5-6 report a pilot study finding 'no mutual intelligibility between Tegem and El Amira speakers'. For Tegem itself: 'Tegem is a tone language' (p.59), six tones, syllable as TBU; no section or statement on stress. No Amira data.

sources.note: Nothing. Publishes the ~70-word El Amira list from Stevenson's mss (ultimately MacDiarmid data) beside Tegem; only phonetic remark is the MacDiarmids' (1931:155) note on the 'strongly pronounced and elongated nature of the vowels' of El Amira (p.4) and that the MacDiarmids' macron 'must represent length' (p.4). No stress, no tone marking for Amira.
